title: ljoss rig document
description:
One saved rig from the ljoss rig designer (one file per rig, `<uuid>.rig.json` in Application Support/RigDesigner/Rigs). Source of truth: ljoss RigDesigner/Model/{Rig,CoreTypes}.swift; written by Store/RigLibrary.swift with JSONEncoder (.sortedKeys, .prettyPrinted, ISO-8601 dates).

Deliberately unlike the namchain document: this is a *tree* — a series of elements, where an element is a block or a parallel section whose lanes are themselves series — so every insertion point is addressable as (container, index) and the canvas renders left-to-right with vertical branches. It is NOT a general DAG.

The namchain engine document is produced from this by DocumentEncoder (RigDesigner/Engine/DocumentEncoder.swift): the tree is flattened into nodes and connections, and BlockMapping.swift decides which catalogue blocks the engine can render and how. See docs/schemas/README.md.

Decoding tolerances: Swift's synthesized Codable ignores unknown keys (so files from newer builds still load), and every field with a default in the model is optional here because the decoder falls back to it when absent. The app's encoder always writes every field; the shape below is what it writes.

name.description: The rig's name, shown in the library.

layout.description: How many chains are drawn. A viewing preference: chains beyond the layout's count are kept, still sent to the engine, and muted visibly.

chains.description: One entry per signal chain (a guitar chain and a vocal chain, say).

paramValue.description: One stored parameter value. The `{"<case>": {"_0": …}}` wrapper is Swift's synthesized Codable encoding of an enum with associated values (ParamValue in CoreTypes.swift). number = a Double knob/level; option = a chosen string; flag = a switch.

values.description: Parameter id → value, only what the user changed: an absent value falls back to the catalogue component's declared default (DocumentEncoder sends the *effective* value). Two reserved keys live here alongside catalogue parameters: "engine.model" and "engine.ir", option values naming assets in the device's library by id.

componentID.description: Catalogue identifier, e.g. "amp.britplexi", "cab.412brit", "delay.tape". A string rather than an enum so a rig saved with a component this build does not know still loads (it renders as an unknown block).

lane.title: Lane

pan.description: -1 (hard left) … 1 (hard right). Stored but never sent: the engine is mono end to end and declares one channel per port.

lane.description: One parallel branch. Its level, mute and polarity reach the engine as a `nc.gain` of the lane's own (linear, so polarity has a sign) because the mixer's per-port level, mute and polarity are runtime state a document cannot set.

splitMode.description: Only yCable reaches today's engine as `nc.split` + `nc.mix`; the others are refused by name rather than quietly flattened into a Y.

crossoverHz.description: Crossover frequency, used only when splitMode is crossover.

balance.description: Routing balance for A/B and dynamic splits, -1 … 1.

lanes.description: After normalize() a section always has ≥ 2 lanes; a single-lane section collapses back into its series, and an all-empty one is pruned.

chainElement.description: One step in the series/parallel tree. The `{"block": {"_0": …}}` / `{"parallel": {"_0": …}}` wrapper is Swift's synthesized Codable for ChainElement.

ioNode.title: IONode
ioNode.description: The fixed endpoints of a chain. Never removable or reorderable, but they carry parameters. Most input/output parameters are deliberately out-of-band (phantom, pad, impedance, destination …) and never sent to the engine; the one that reaches it is the output level, as a `nc.gain` node.

source.description: What the chain is for; decides which device channels it binds to by position (first chain → channel 0, and so on).
